items.title: 6.1.1 Parametric Equations of a Circle (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 164-165: parametric equations x = r cos(theta), y = r sin(theta) with Figure 6.3; Examples 1 and 2

blocks.text: Is sabaq mein hum circle ko ek naye tareeqe se likhna seekhenge: parametric equations. Ab tak circle ki equation \(x\) aur \(y\) ka aik rishta thi. Ab hum har point ko ek hi number, angle \(\theta\), se batayenge. Yeh tareeqa aage tangent, normal aur ellipse wagaira mein bohat kaam aata hai, is liye ise dil laga kar samajhiye.

blocks.alt: Circle with centre O(0, 0). P(x, y) on the circle joined to O by radius r making angle theta with the x-axis; PM is perpendicular to the x-axis, forming right triangle OMP.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.3: the point P(x, y) on the circle and the angle theta (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text:
Maan lijiye \(P(x, y)\) circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}\) par koi bhi point hai, aur \(\overline{OP}\) ka inclination (positive \(x\)-axis se angle) \(\theta\) hai, jaisa Figure 6.3 mein dikhaya gaya hai. \(P\) se \(x\)-axis par perpendicular \(\overline{PM}\) khenchiye. Ab \(OMP\) ek right triangle hai (M par 90 degree), aur right triangle mein trigonometric ratios ki definition yaad kijiye: cos = saath wali side / hypotenuse, sin = saamne wali side / hypotenuse. Is liye
\[\cos\theta = \dfrac{|\overline{OM}|}{|\overline{OP}|}\]
\[\sin\theta = \dfrac{|\overline{PM}|}{|\overline{OP}|}\]
Ab dekhiye: \(|\overline{OM}| = x\) (P ka horizontal faasla), \(|\overline{PM}| = y\) (P ki unchai) aur \(|\overline{OP}| = r\) (radius). Is liye
\[\cos\theta = \dfrac{x}{r}, \quad \sin\theta = \dfrac{y}{r}\]
Dono ko \(r\) se multiply karne par circle ki parametric equations milti hain:

blocks.text_alt: x equals r cos theta, y equals r sin theta

blocks.text: Point \(P(r\cos\theta, r\sin\theta)\) har \(\theta\) ke liye circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}\) par hota hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Parameter ek madadgaar variable hai. Circle ko \(x\) aur \(y\) ki ek equation se batane ke bajaye hum har point ko ek number \(\theta\) se batate hain. Socho ek ghari ki sui: sui ka angle bata do to sui ki nok ki jagah maloom ho jati hai. Bilkul isi tarah \(\theta\) bata do to point maloom. Jab \(\theta\) \(0\) se \(2\pi\) (0 se 360 degree) tak chalta hai to point \((r\cos\theta, r\sin\theta)\) circle ka ek poora chakkar laga leta hai.
Yeh point circle par kyun hai? Equation mein rakh kar dekhiye aur \(\cos^{2}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta = 1\) istemal kijiye:
\[r^{2}\cos^{2}\theta + r^{2}\sin^{2}\theta = r^{2}\]
Figure mein \(P\) pehle quadrant mein dikhaya gaya hai, magar formulas har quadrant mein sahi hain, kyun ke \(\cos\theta\) aur \(\sin\theta\) ke signs khud hi \(x\) aur \(y\) ke sahi signs de dete hain.
Agar centre \((h, k)\) ho to isi idea se \(x = h + r\cos\theta\), \(y = k + r\sin\theta\) milta hai (yani origin wale circle ko \((h, k)\) tak khiska do). Yeh Exercise 6.2 mein kaam aayega.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 16\) par \(\theta = 90^{\circ}\) wala point kaun sa hai? (\(x = 4\cos 90^{\circ} = 0\), \(y = 4\sin 90^{\circ} = 4\), yani \((0, 4)\): bilkul upar wala point.)
Ab kitab ki do misaalein dekhte hain. Pehli bilkul seedhi hai: centre aur radius se equation likhna. Doosri mein parameter khatam kar ke locus nikaalna hai.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.problem: Write an equation of the circle with centre \((-2, 1)\) and radius 5.
steps:
Diya gaya: centre \((-2, 1)\), radius \(5\).
Maloom karna: circle ki equation.
Tareeqa: sab se pehle dekhte hain ke sawal mein kya diya hai: centre aur radius dono seedhe diye hain. Jab yeh dono maloom hon to standard form (Theorem 1) bilkul fit baithti hai; koi aur tareeqa dhoondne ki zaroorat hi nahin.

Step 1: h, k aur r pehchaanein
\[h = -2, \quad k = 1, \quad r = 5\]
Kyun: standard form \((x - h)^{2} + (y - k)^{2} = r^{2}\) ko yahi teen numbers chahiyein. Centre ka pehla coordinate \(h\), doosra \(k\).

Step 2: Standard form mein rakhein
\[(x - (-2))^{2} + (y - 1)^{2} = 5^{2}\]
\[(x + 2)^{2} + (y - 1)^{2} = 25\]
Kyun: negative number ko minus karna us ko jama karna hai, is liye \(x - (-2) = x + 2\).
Dhyan dein: yahin sab se zyada ghalti hoti hai. Centre ka coordinate negative ho to bracket mein plus aata hai.

Step 3: Khol kar kitab wali shakal mein likhein
\[x^{2} + 4x + 4 + y^{2} - 2y + 1 = 25\]
\[x^{2} + y^{2} + 4x - 2y - 20 = 0\]
Kyun: \((x + 2)^{2} = x^{2} + 4x + 4\) aur \((y - 1)^{2} = y^{2} - 2y + 1\); phir constants jama karein: \(4 + 1 - 25 = -20\). Kitab jawab isi khuli hui (general) shakal mein deti hai.

Tasdeeq:
Ab ulta chal kar dekhte hain. \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\) (6.1.2) se muqabla karein: \(g = 2\), \(f = -1\), \(c = -20\).
\[\text{centre} = (-g, -f) = (-2, 1)\]
\[r = \sqrt{4 + 1 + 20} = 5\]
Dono wahi aaye jo sawal mein diye the, is liye jawab durust hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Example 2 locus ka sawal hai. Locus yani woh raasta jis par koi chalta hua point rehta hai. Aise sawalon ka pattern yaad kar lijiye: (1) point kisi parameter (yahan \(\theta\)) ke zariye diya hota hai; (2) parameter ko khatam karo; (3) jo \(x\) aur \(y\) ki equation bache, wahi locus hai. Jab \(\theta\) \(\cos\theta\) aur \(\sin\theta\) ki jori ki shakal mein aaye, to square kar ke jama karna sab se aazmooda (tried and tested) chaal hai.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.problem: Prove that the locus of the point of intersection of the lines \(x\cos\theta + y\sin\theta = a\), \(x\sin\theta - y\cos\theta = b\) is a circle with centre at \((0, 0)\) and radius \(\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\), where \(\theta\) is a parameter.
steps:
Diya gaya: do lines \(x\cos\theta + y\sin\theta = a\) aur \(x\sin\theta - y\cos\theta = b\), jin mein \(\theta\) badalta rehta hai.
Maloom karna (saabit karna): in ka intersection point (milne ki jagah) hamesha ek circle par hota hai jis ka centre \((0, 0)\) aur radius \(\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\) hai.
Tareeqa: locus (woh raasta jis par point chalta hai) nikaalne ke liye parameter \(\theta\) ko khatam (eliminate) karte hain. Yahan square kar ke jama karna kaam karega, kyun ke \(\cos^{2}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta = 1\) wali identity \(\theta\) ko gayab kar degi.

Step 1: Dono equations ka square le kar jama karein
\[(x\cos\theta + y\sin\theta)^{2}\]
\[+ (x\sin\theta - y\cos\theta)^{2}\]
\[= a^{2} + b^{2}\]
Kyun: intersection point dono equations ko ek saath satisfy karta hai, is liye dono left sides ke squares ka jama \(a^{2} + b^{2}\) ke barabar hoga.

Step 2: Har square ko kholein
\[(x\cos\theta + y\sin\theta)^{2}\]
\[= x^{2}\cos^{2}\theta + 2xy\cos\theta\sin\theta\]
\[+ y^{2}\sin^{2}\theta\]
\[(x\sin\theta - y\cos\theta)^{2}\]
\[= x^{2}\sin^{2}\theta - 2xy\sin\theta\cos\theta\]
\[+ y^{2}\cos^{2}\theta\]
Kyun: \((p + q)^{2} = p^{2} + 2pq + q^{2}\) aur \((p - q)^{2} = p^{2} - 2pq + q^{2}\). Beech wale terms ek plus aur ek minus hain, is liye jama karte hi cancel ho jate hain. Isi liye sawal mein doosri line mein minus rakha gaya hai.

Step 3: \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) wale terms ikatthe karein
\[x^{2}(\cos^{2}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta)\]
\[+ y^{2}(\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta) = a^{2} + b^{2}\]
Kyun: common factor bahar nikaalne se dono terms mein ek hi bracket aa jati hai, aur woh bracket humein pehchani hui hai.

Step 4: \(\cos^{2}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta = 1\) lagayein
\[x^{2}(1) + y^{2}(1) = a^{2} + b^{2}\]
\[x^{2} + y^{2} = \left(\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\right)^{2}\]
Kyun: identity ne \(\theta\) ko bilkul khatam kar diya; ab sirf \(x\) aur \(y\) ka rishta bacha hai, aur yahi locus hai.

Step 5: Locus pehchaanein
Is ko \(x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}\) (6.1 ka Note (iii)) se milayein: yeh circle hai jis ka centre \((0, 0)\) aur radius \(\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\) hai.
Kyun: right side ko poore square ki shakal mein likhne se radius seedha nazar aa jata hai.

Tasdeeq:
Ek misaal le kar dekhte hain: \(a = 3\), \(b = 4\), \(\theta = 0\). Tab lines \(x = 3\) aur \(-y = 4\) ban jati hain, jo \((3, -4)\) par milti hain.
\[3^{2} + (-4)^{2} = 25 = 3^{2} + 4^{2}\]
Yani point radius \(\sqrt{25} = 5\) wale circle par hai, bilkul jaisa saabit kiya.
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: locus \(x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}\) hai, yani circle jis ka centre \((0, 0)\) aur radius \(\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\) hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin.) Point \((5\cos t, 5\sin t)\) ka locus kya hai?
\(x = 5\cos t\), \(y = 5\sin t\). Dono ka square le kar jama karein:
\[x^{2} + y^{2} = 25(\cos^{2}t + \sin^{2}t) = 25\]
Locus: circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 25\), centre origin, radius 5. Dekha? Parametric se seedhi equation tak pohanchne ka bhi yahi square-aur-jama wala tareeqa hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}\) ki parametric equations: \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(y = r\sin\theta\).
2. \(\theta\) woh angle hai jo \(\overline{OP}\) positive \(x\)-axis ke saath banata hai; \(0 \le \theta < 2\pi\) mein poora circle ban jata hai.
3. Centre aur radius diye hon to foran standard form likhiye (Example 1).
4. Parameter wala locus: parameter khatam karo; \(\cos\theta\), \(\sin\theta\) ki jori ho to square kar ke jama karo (Example 2).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Ulta jor dena: \(x\) ke saath \(\cos\theta\) aur \(y\) ke saath \(\sin\theta\) aata hai (angle \(x\)-axis se naapa jata hai).
2. Centre mein sign ki ghalti: centre \((-2, 1)\) ho to \((x + 2)^{2}\) aata hai, \((x - 2)^{2}\) nahin.
3. \((x\cos\theta + y\sin\theta)^{2}\) kholte waqt beech wala term bhool jana; yeh dono squares jama karne ke baad hi cancel hota hai, pehle nahin.
